assessmentSummary.identity: From a seated tuck on a clean, stable mat or floor, hold the shins, keep the body compact and rounded, rock backward only to the upper-back/shoulder contact range that remains controlled, rock forward, bring both feet under the body, and stand tall without placing hands on the floor or another person. One complete seated-tuck to tall-standing return is one cycle. Repeated tuck rocks that return to seated, any hand or partner assistance, raised surfaces, forward or backward rolls, a hand-supported backward-roll action, and different terminal positions are separate tasks or reviewed variants.
currentCardFindings: Source 81 establishes seated tuck, rocking on the upper back/shoulders, a feet-under-body transition, and tall standing finish but lacks an exact repetition unit, no-hand boundary, quality gates, dosage, fatigue, media review, relationships, and calibration.

The exact candidate uses a no-hand floor return because hand support or a partner changes contacts, assistance, force path, logistics, and coaching needs. Those changes cannot be silently treated as participant-skill labels.

Three direct legacy YouTube URLs are retained only as unverified, non-embedded candidates. Search and source presence do not verify playback, exact cycle match, safety, captions, accessibility, quality, reviewer, or approval.

proposedLoadProfile.recovery: candidate planning estimate only; recompute from actual cycles, contact tolerance, symptoms, assistance, surface, and overlapping rolling or squat work

proposedDosage.rest: 30-90 seconds or enough to restore compact tuck, controlled upper-back contact, feet-under-body return, breathing, and balance
proposedDosage.durationRule: include floor setup, demonstration, valid and failed cycles, rest, substitutions, cleaning, and controlled exit

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only when the exact no-hand seated tuck-rock-to-tall cycle, stable floor/mat, clear exit, communication, head/neck and upper-back contact tolerance, cumulative fatigue, duration, logistics, and downstream work fit. Tuck compactness, pace, cycles, rest, mat use, and cueing are delivery annotations only while the exact contact path and no-hand tall finish remain. Hand support, partner assistance, raised or inclined surface, repeated seated rocks, forward/backward roll, different finish, assessment, or clinical intent requires revalidation.

calibrationEvidence.basis: Source 81 lineage, published gymnastics rolling teaching guidance, task mechanics, and comparison with tuck rocks, assisted rock-to-stand, forward/backward rolls, and squat-roll-to-stand.
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No source establishes universal contact range, cycle count, recovery, readiness, clearance, outcome, transfer, or Vortex score. Independent human calibration remains required.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Start seated in a compact tuck on a clean stable mat or floor, holding the shins. Rock backward only to controlled upper-back and shoulder contact, rock forward, place both feet under the body, and stand tall without placing hands on the floor or another person. One seated-tuck to tall-standing return is one cycle. Hand or partner assistance, raised surfaces, repeated rocks returning to seated, forward or backward rolls, changed terminal positions, assessment, and clinical intervention require separate reviewed variants or definitions.
